title: La bulla
desc: A speaker on the pavement at one in the morning
setting: The neighbour's music has been going since nine and you have come out to the acera, where doña Chepa is already sitting.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Ideay, ¿y usted despierto a esta hora?
steps.en: Ideay, and you awake at this hour?

options.en: With that racket, doña, who is sleeping?
options.feedback: Bulla is not a complaint word here, it is a weather word. Saying it like that puts you on the pavement with her instead of above it.

options.es: No puedo dormir con ese ruido.
options.en: I cannot sleep with that noise.
options.feedback: True, and ruido is the neutral word. Bulla is the one this street uses and it carries no accusation.
You are five years in and proposing a law about the neighbour's speaker. Doña Chepa will remember that sentence.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Es el cumpleaños de la nieta. Una vez al año, pues.
steps.en: It is the granddaughter's birthday. Once a year, after all.

options.es: Ah, con razón. Entonces que la pasen bien.
options.en: Ah, that explains it. Let them enjoy it, then.
options.feedback: The reason changes everything and it always exists. Once you have it, the noise stops being an offence and becomes somebody's party.

options.es: No sabía. Ya al menos entiendo.
options.en: I did not know. At least now I understand.
options.feedback: Fair. Half a step short of wishing them well, which is the part that gets repeated tomorrow.

options.es: Una vez al año hasta las tres de la mañana.
options.en: Once a year until three in the morning.
options.feedback: She gave you the reason so that you would let it go. Answering with the hour tells her you have not.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Mi hija dice que a las doce lo bajan. Vamos a ver.
steps.en: My daughter says they will turn it down at twelve. We will see.

options.es: Vamos a ver, doña. Aquí me quedo un rato con usted.
options.en: We will see, doña. I will sit out here with you a while.
options.feedback: Vamos a ver means it is not happening and both of you know it. Sitting down instead of going in is the only real solution anybody has found.
Kind. It will not go down at twelve and she was warning you rather than promising.

options.es: ¿Y si les pedimos que le bajen?
options.en: And what if we ask them to turn it down?
options.feedback: Nobody asks. It is a fifteen-year-old's birthday and asking makes an enemy on a street you will live on for another twenty years.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: Al principio usted no aguantaba nada de bulla. ¿Se acuerda?
steps.en: At the start you could not stand any noise at all. Do you remember?

options.es: La primera noche no dormí nada, doña. Ya ni la oigo.
options.en: The first night I did not sleep at all, doña. Now I do not even hear it.
options.feedback: That is the whole five years in one sentence. The noise was the first thing that nearly sent you home, and you stopped noticing it some year you cannot name.

options.en: Yes, I got used to it.
options.feedback: True. She asked because she has been watching it happen and wanted to hear you say it.

options.es: Todavía no me acostumbro del todo.
options.en: I am still not entirely used to it.
options.feedback: Honest, and you are sitting on a pavement at one in the morning talking to a neighbour instead of lying awake being angry. That is used to it.
